title: Benign ovarian masses: functional cysts, mature cystic teratoma, ovarian torsion and RMI scoring
subject: ss-obg
refs: Gynecology by Ten Teachers 21e Ch 15 (Benign diseases of the ovary)
RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 62: Management of Suspected Ovarian Masses in Premenopausal Women
ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 174: Evaluation and Management of Adnexal Masses

steps.say: Functional ovarian cysts represent the most common adnexal enlargements in women of reproductive age. Arising from unruptured Graafian follicles or failing corpus luteum involution, physiological cysts typically measure under five centimeters in diameter and regress spontaneously over two to three cycles.
steps.tx: **Functional ovarian cysts** (follicular and corpus luteum cysts) represent physiological distensions arising during normal ovulatory cycles. Characteristically unilocular, thin-walled, and measuring < 5 cm, the vast majority undergo complete **spontaneous regression** within 8 to 12 weeks of expectant follow-up without requiring surgical intervention.

steps.say: Mature cystic teratoma is the most frequent benign ovarian neoplasm encountered in young reproductive-age women. Originating from totipotent germ cells, these benign tumors contain tissues from ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm, exhibiting hair, teeth, bone, and sebaceous material within a Rokitansky protuberance.
steps.tx: **Mature cystic teratoma** (dermoid cyst) is the most prevalent benign ovarian neoplasm in women under 40 years. Derived from totipotent **germ cells**, it contains well-differentiated tissues from all 3 germ cell layers (skin, sebaceous glands, teeth, bone), characteristically concentrated in a mural **Rokitansky protuberance**.

rows: Fat-fluid level on pelvic MRI or CT scan

steps.say: Specialized monodermal transformation of a mature teratoma can produce functionally active thyroid tissue within the ovary. Struma ovarii is diagnosed when mature thyroid tissue comprises more than fifty percent of the mass, occasionally presenting with clinical thyrotoxicosis.
steps.tx: **Struma ovarii** is a specialized monodermal teratoma where mature functional **thyroid tissue** constitutes > 50 percent of the neoplasm. Approximately 5 to 10 percent of affected patients present with overt clinical **hyperthyroidism** and an adnexal mass, completely curable by surgical cystectomy or unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy.

left.title: Classic Mature Cystic Teratoma
points: Contains mixed tissues from ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm
High lipid and sebum content; Rokitansky protuberance
Rare malignant transformation (1-2%, usually squamous carcinoma)

right.title: Struma Ovarii (Monodermal Teratoma)
points: Predominantly composed of mature thyroid parenchyma (> 50%)
May cause thyrotoxicosis with low radioiodine neck uptake

steps.say: Serous and mucinous cystadenomas represent the most common benign epithelial ovarian neoplasms. Serous cystadenomas are characteristically unilocular with smooth inner linings, while mucinous cystadenomas are multilocular, filled with thick gelatinous fluid, and reach immense dimensions.
steps.tx: Benign epithelial neoplasms comprise **serous cystadenoma** (unilocular, thin-walled, filled with watery serous fluid and lined by ciliated cuboidal cells) and **mucinous cystadenoma** (multilocular, partitioned by multiple thin septations, and filled with thick viscous mucin produced by endocervical-like tall columnar cells).

rows: Unilocular or few compartments, smooth external surface
Multilocular with numerous thin internal daughter cysts
Clear, thin, watery straw-colored serous fluid
Ciliated columnar cells resembling fallopian tube
Tall non-ciliated columnar cells with basal nuclei
Benign peritoneal fluid resorption without sequelae

steps.say: Ovarian torsion is a gynecological surgical emergency caused by partial or complete twisting of the adnexa around its vascular pedicle. Twisting of the infundibulopelvic and utero-ovarian ligaments causes initial low-pressure venous and lymphatic thrombosis, rapidly progressing to arterial occlusion and hemorrhagic infarction.
steps.tx: **Ovarian torsion** is an acute gynecological emergency where the adnexa twists along the axis of the **infundibulopelvic ligament** and utero-ovarian ligament. Early obstruction of low-pressure **venous outflow** produces massive stromal edema, progressing rapidly to **arterial occlusion**, tissue gangrene, and hemorrhagic adnexal infarction.

nodes.label: Adnexal mass (5 to 10 cm, benign teratoma) twists on its pedicle
Early venous and lymphatic obstruction causes severe adnexal edema
Progressive twisting obstructs arterial inflow leading to ischemic pain
Emergency laparoscopy: detorsion and ovarian preservation

steps.say: Color Doppler sonography demonstrates the pathognomonic whirlpool sign of twisted vascular pedicles in adnexal torsion. However, the presence of detectable arterial Doppler flow does not reliably exclude ovarian torsion due to dual arterial supply from the uterine and ovarian vessels.
steps.tx: Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates an enlarged, hyperechoic, edematous stroma with peripherally displaced follicles and the pathognomonic **whirlpool sign** of twisted vessels on **Doppler ultrasound**. Critically, the documented presence of arterial Doppler signals does **not rule out torsion** in acute surgical presentations.

left.title: Positive Ultrasound Signs of Torsion
points: Enlarged ovary (> 4 to 5 cm or > 20 mL volume)
Peripherally displaced small antral follicles ('string of pearls')
Direct visualization of twisted pedicle: whirlpool sign

right.title: Diagnostic Pitfall of Doppler Flow
points: Dual arterial supply (ovarian artery and uterine branch)
Arterial flow persists in up to 30 to 40 percent of surgically proven torsions
Normal Doppler should never delay emergency surgical intervention

steps.say: Modern surgical doctrine prioritises conservative laparoscopic detorsion over immediate oophorectomy, even in cyanotic, ischemic ovaries. Adnexal untwisting restores microvascular perfusion in over ninety percent of cases without increasing systemic pulmonary thromboembolism risks.
steps.tx: Current surgical consensus mandates **laparoscopic detorsion** with ovarian conservation rather than immediate oophorectomy, regardless of dark cyanotic discoloration. Detorsion preserves viable follicular reserve in over 90 percent of cases without increasing the clinical risk of **pulmonary embolism** or systemic thrombotic complications.

nodes.label: Perform emergency diagnostic laparoscopy under general anesthesia
Carefully untwist ischemic adnexal pedicle using atraumatic graspers
Observe for return of perfusion, tissue pinking, and venous reperfusion
Perform simple cystectomy or postpone cystectomy until edema resolves

steps.say: The Risk of Malignancy Index combines serum CA-125 concentration, ultrasound features, and menopausal status to differentiate benign adnexal masses from malignancy. An RMI score of 200 or greater demonstrates over eighty percent sensitivity for ovarian carcinoma, mandating gynecological oncology referral.
steps.tx: The **Risk of Malignancy Index** (RMI-1) calculates risk as: Ultrasound score (U) x Menopausal score (M) x **serum CA-125** level. An **RMI score** of 200 or higher carries an 85 percent sensitivity for ovarian malignancy, serving as the international triage cutoff for gynecological oncology referral.
